newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK RATE FALL SEEN AS SHORT-TERM PHENOMENON.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK RATE FALL SEEN AS SHORT-TERM PHENOMENON.

text.p: Slovak short-term interbank money rates fell below 20 percent on Tuesday with most banks appearing to have enough liquidity to meet minimum reserves requirements (PMR) later in the day, dealers said.

One-day funds eased to 10-15 percent after opening at 20 percent, but traders said the decline was a short-term phenomenon and that rates were likely to climb back to around 20 percent in coming days.
"This was a short-term move. Tomorrow's rates are again at 20 percent," said Tatra banka's chief dealer Jozef Bozek.
Bozek said he expected most maturities to hover between 20-30 percent in the near future.
Traders said the development of rates would depend on central bank (NBS) moves to add liquidity through repo tenders.
"If the NBS keeps adding crowns and helps the sector stay above 100 percent of PMR, rates may ease to 15 to 20 percent," Bozek said.

Rastislav Zivor, of ING Bank, said NBS moves to increase liquidity revived trading with funds longer than one-day. "There were some trades with one-month and three-month money with rates at around 23 to 28 percent," he said.
Some dealers said foreign funds had started to return to the interbank market, playing on the interest rate differential though it was hard to estimate the volumes.
Most Slovak banks are expected to meet their PMR on Tuesday with the entire sector seen to end this PMR period with between 99.85 and 100 percent of PMR funds needed.
